title: House in Beloura / ARX Portugal Arquitectos
text:
House in Beloura / ARX Portugal Arquitectos

The house is positioned on the site with the aim of responding in a relatively simple way to two central questions: How can it capture a panoramic view of the horizon, which also brings us the presence of the sea? How can it embrace outdoor spaces that simultaneously protect the residents' privacy from neighbors' views and ensure comfort on days of strong wind?

title: French Creek Workshops House / Wittman Estes
text:
French Creek Workshops House / Wittman Estes

This home for a newly retired couple sits beside a wetland on a four-and-a-half-acre site once used as an animal sanctuary. Conceived as a serene retreat immersed in nature, it offers comfort and beauty throughout the seasons, sheltering its occupants during the cool, rainy months and opening outward during the dry, warm season.

title: MKR Store in Seville / Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra
text:
MKR Store in Seville / Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra

The refurbishment Project for the multilabel shop MKR arises from the demand of reorganizing and giving a new image to the existing retail space: an unstructured and limited space, not in compliance with the actual regulatory standards.

title: Rustoordlaan / Atelier M Architects + Planners bv
text:
Rustoordlaan / Atelier M Architects + Planners bv

Nestled within Heuvelhofpark in Kessel-Lo (BE) lies the new replacement housing project for the social housing company Dijledal. To maximize the preservation of the existing trees and the park, the building's footprint was kept highly compact and rotated 17 degrees. Wrapped in light green terracotta panels and finished with reseda green windows, the 30 units offer residents the ultimate luxury: a living experience right up among the treetops.

title: Human-Centered Design: How does design shape the way we live, feel, and connect?
text:
Human-Centered Design: How does design shape the way we live, feel, and connect?

To say that we design "for people" seems like a fundamental premise of architecture. However, this statement presents a problem: people are not a homogeneous category.

Human-Centered Design invites us to question whom we observe, listen to, and represent when making design decisions. Through an interdisciplinary conversation, we will explore how physical, sensory, and social needs influence architecture and interior design, and how these shape our way of living, feeling, and connecting.

Drawing from the fields of health, air transport, education, urban planning, and architectural representation, various perspectives will bring these priorities into dialogue.

title: The Invisible Brief: How Laboratory Needs Shape Research Buildings
text:
The Invisible Brief: How Laboratory Needs Shape Research Buildings

A floor that feels solid may still be moving. Vibrations travel through the ground and across buildings, often at levels too small for people to notice. Most have little effect on everyday activities, but in some research laboratories, instruments measuring matter at the nanoscale can register movements this small, and even traffic several miles away can interfere with an experiment.

title: Black Miller House / Three Sixty Architecture
text:
Black Miller House / Three Sixty Architecture

Black Miller House is conceived as a cluster of contemporary pavilions embedded within a 32-hectare coastal hill landscape. The design retains much of the existing dwelling while introducing new living and sleeping wings, creating a relaxed, climate-responsive retreat that feels grounded in the land and open to the expansive outlook. Rather than replacing the original structure, the project adopts a strategy of selective demolition, retention, and expansion, allowing the building to evolve while respecting its historical presence on the site.

title: Latin America in Focus: This Month in Architecture, Social Housing, and Heritage Recovery
text:
Latin America in Focus: This Month in Architecture, Social Housing, and Heritage Recovery

This October, architecture across Latin America became a platform for exchange, bringing together discussions on inhabitation, cultural identity, emerging practices, and the relationship between the built environment and its wider context. From conversations on emerging architectural practices and material research at Design Week Mexico to new approaches to housing, landscape, and public space in Chile and Mexico, recent developments highlight how architecture responds to specific local conditions. Across the region, initiatives addressing climate adaptation and heritage recovery in the Dominican Republic and Colombia also bring attention to the changing responsibilities of cultural institutions and the built environment.

title: Súria Library / Javier de las Heras Solé
text:
Súria Library / Javier de las Heras Solé

A public space for gathering and meeting. Through repetition and pattern, this project proposes an architecture that eschews gratuitous gestures, one in which the focus is on the citizen and the ways in which they use the space. It is an architecture that recognizes and highlights existing physical, heritage, and cultural elements, integrating itself into the context and fostering the collective appropriation of the place.

title: The Architecture Drawing Prize Announces 11 Recipients for Its 2026 Edition
text:
The Architecture Drawing Prize Announces 11 Recipients for Its 2026 Edition

Launched in 2017, The Architecture Drawing Prize is organized annually to celebrate and showcase the art of architectural drawing across multiple formats and techniques. Co-curated by Make Architects, Sir John Soane's Museum and the World Architecture Festival (WAF), and supported by Iris Ceramica Group with ArchDaily as media partner, the ninth edition has announced the 11 recipients. This year, the drawings were selected from 168 entries from around the world, with a special prize for hand-drawing. An overall recipient will be announced at Sir John Soane's Museum in London in early 2027, where The Architecture Drawing Prize exhibition will run from January 27 to February 28, 2027.

title: Time Space Existence 2027 Asks What It Means to Design with Change
text:
Time Space Existence 2027 Asks What It Means to Design with Change

The architecture biennial exhibition Time Space Existence returns for its 8th edition with more than 200 participants, from established global firms to emerging studios and academic institutions. Their work will be presented across three historic venues in Venice: Palazzo Mora, Palazzo Bembo and the Marinaressa Gardens. Many have already been confirmed, and the curatorial team is finalising the line-up.

title: The Work of Keeping a Public Building Public: The Drill Hall in Johannesburg
text:
The Work of Keeping a Public Building Public: The Drill Hall in Johannesburg

What happens to a building after the architecture is finished? For buildings intended to serve the public, their continued life depends on more than the physical conditions of their construction. It involves the activities that take place within them, the relationships they allow to develop, the people who occupy and shape them, and the institutional structures responsible for their upkeep. Yet these conditions are not always secured through the act of building itself. They are continually negotiated, often through forms of work that remain outside the conventional understanding of architectural practice.

title: Villa Sahar / Mahfoud Laasri Architecte - MLA
text:
Villa Sahar / Mahfoud Laasri Architecte - MLA

Sahar is a private residence in Casablanca conceived around the interplay of mass and lightness, materiality and transparency, and architecture and landscape. Its name, derived from the Arabic word سَحَر, refers to the moment just before dawn. The principal facade faces east, making morning light an essential part of the project's identity and an inspiration for its architectural expression.

title: Funamoto Dental Clinic / STUDIO ALUC
text:
Funamoto Dental Clinic / STUDIO ALUC

This project is a newly built dental clinic located in Uchinada, Ishikawa Prefecture. STUDIO ALUC was responsible for the design as a whole, from architecture to interior spaces and custom furniture. Strong winds sweeping in from the Sea of Japan and the overcast skies of Hokuriku—guided by this climate and an irregular triangular site, the architecture takes the form of four staggered volumes.

title: Hotel Amares / Cel-Ras Arquitectura
text:
Hotel Amares / Cel-Ras Arquitectura

Amares stands on a 14,152 m² beachfront site on Playa El Estillero, near El Limón, on the northern coast of the Samaná Peninsula in the Dominican Republic. The plot lies between the Atlantic and a backdrop of coconut palms and tropical forest, in one of the few stretches of Caribbean coast still free from large-scale tourism.

title: House Toca / ARKITITO Arquitetura
text:
House Toca / ARKITITO Arquitetura

Going against the grain of a traditional residence, Casa Toca emerges from a diverse program that includes domestic spaces, an art studio, a music studio, and areas for gatherings — reflecting the lifestyle of its residents, architect Tito Ficarelli and visual artist Luiza Gottschalk, who are also responsible for the design. This is the third home conceived and built by the couple for different stages of their life together.

title: The Vineyard HOUSE? / Lauti Esain
text:
The Vineyard HOUSE? / Lauti Esain

The Vineyard ?HOUSE? On September 10, 2022, at 12:29 p.m., I broke ground with the first of thousands of shovels I would dig to build my house. But the story began in my second year of architecture school, when I lost my parents. That was when I started working and saving, just in case something happened to me. Then, a dream emerged: to live on a vineyard. I decided that if I didn't need to use those savings upon graduating, I would use them to build my house. When I graduated, my savings were enough for 215 sq ft (20 m²), but by building it with my own hands, I could save on labor costs and reach 355 sq ft (33 m²).

title: House Around a Column / fala
text:
House Around a Column / fala

The compact plot sits within a dense piece of urban fabric, surrounded on all sides by neighbouring houses. Its shape is skewed. The project begins with the challenge of inscribing a house into this distorted figure. The longest wall of the plot becomes the guide. From it, a set of geometric rules gradually unfolds, quietly organising the plan.

title: Understory House / Gluck+
text:
Understory House / Gluck+

Set on a long, gentle slope in the foothills of the Catskill Mountains, Understory House takes its name from its precise position within the forest—neither rooted on the forest floor nor lifted above the canopy, but suspended in between, where the midstory becomes the primary experience. Located in a rural second-growth forest marked by miles of historic stone walls, the 3,170-square-foot house responds directly to the character and memory of the land.

title: SFJ6 Building / MARMOLBRAVO + MADhel
text:
SFJ6 Building / MARMOLBRAVO + MADhel

SFJ6 is a project of 102 dwellings designed to adapt to the complexity of the city, solving several urban problems and generating quality public spaces in its surroundings. The building is integrated into the city as a folded volume that embraces the disparate existing buildings, taking special care of the contact areas and adapting its ground floor to the complex topography of the site in order to generate the greatest points of contact with the city and revitalize the public space.

title: Atrapos, Summer Residence on the Island of Antiparos / AREA
text:
Atrapos, Summer Residence on the Island of Antiparos / AREA

The sinuous curves of the house unfold along an old, agrarian pathway, closely following the natural contours of the earth. As the plan gently steps down the glen, sectional differences begin to organize the interior, and the single-level residence gradually settles into its position as a subterranean dwelling.
